source: arXiv:2603.16365 — FactorEngine: A Program-level Knowledge-Infused Factor Mining Framework. Lin et al., March 2026 (updated April 9, 2026).
title: R33 Concept: FactorEngine-style LLM-guided Factor Mining from Financial Reports
rationale: FactorEngine (arXiv:2603.16365, March 2026) introduces a multi-agent system that converts unstructured financial research reports into executable Python factor programs, then uses LLM-guided + Bayesian search to discover superior alpha factors. On CSI300 (China), achieves Sharpe 1.0093 vs Alpha158 baselines — +58% IC and +126% excess return. Architecture: (1) Multi-agent report extraction: PDF → structured JSON → pseudocode → executable Python; (2) LLM-guided directional search for logic revision; (3) Bayesian optimization for parameter tuning; (4) Experience base enabling trajectory-aware refinement. Downside: tested only on Chinese markets (CSI300/CSI500); uses Gemini-2.5-Pro (API cost); no public code. Applicability to US equity market R33 concept: The 'financial research reports → factors' pipeline is generalizable. A US adaptation would seed with: (a) our existing 146 harness strategies as seed factors, (b) publicly available academic research summaries (SSRN abstracts) as knowledge source, (c) GPT-4o or Claude Haiku as LLM backbone. This is an R33+ concept — not immediately actionable but worth recording as a concrete architecture reference.
content:
### FactorEngine: LLM-Guided Factor Mining from Financial Reports (arXiv:2603.16365, March 2026)
- **Paper**: Lin et al. 'FactorEngine: A Program-level Knowledge-Infused Factor Mining Framework for Quantitative Investment.' arXiv:2603.16365, March 2026 (updated April 9, 2026).
- **Market tested**: CSI300 and CSI500 (China A-shares), out-of-sample 2017-2024
- **Key results vs Alpha158 baseline**: CSI300: IC 0.0474 vs ~0.030, ICIR 0.3185, AR 18.99%, Sharpe 1.0093, MaxDD 12.61%. +58% IC improvement, +126% excess annualized return.
- **Architecture**: (1) Multi-agent PDF pipeline: financial research reports → structured JSON → pseudocode → executable Python factors; (2) LLM-guided directional search (logic revision) + Bayesian optimization (parameters); (3) Experience base that enables trajectory-aware refinement from prior failures.
- **LLM used**: Gemini-2.5-Pro (primary); ablations with GPT-4o and Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite.
- **Limitation**: China-focused; no public code; API costs (Gemini-2.5-Pro).
- **R33+ concept for US adaptation**: Seed with (a) 146 harness strategies as initial factor pool, (b) SSRN abstract summaries as knowledge documents, (c) Claude Haiku as backbone. Use FactorEngine's separation of 'logic revision (LLM)' vs 'parameter tuning (Bayesian)' as the core design principle.
- **Contrast with Alpha-R1** (arXiv:2512.23515): Alpha-R1 uses RL to gate existing factors; FactorEngine uses LLM+search to GENERATE new factors. Complementary approaches — R33 should evaluate both.
